transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

I can't tell you exactly which part to buy yet because I don't know if it's a simple blockage or a failed component. However, on a Beko vented dryer that is 6 years old, the most common cause of 'drum turns but no heat' is actually a blocked filter. When the lint filter or condenser gets clogged with fluff, airflow stops. The dryer overheats and trips a safety switch (thermal cut-out) to prevent fire, which cuts the heat immediately. This often happens even if you haven't noticed it getting very hot because the air just feels cold coming out. Before looking for parts, please do this:
1. Unplug the machine.
2. Remove the lint filter from the door frame and clean it thoroughly under a tap if needed.
3. Open the small flap at the bottom front of the machine to reveal the condenser unit. Take it out and rinse off all the fluff under the tap. Let it drip dry completely before putting it back.
4. Check the vent hose at the back is not kinked or blocked. Once you've done that, plug it back in and run a normal heat programme for 10 minutes. Does it start heating now? If the filters were already clean, or if cleaning them didn't fix it, then the heater element or thermal cut-out has likely failed internally, and we would need to look at replacing those parts.
Done all that. Filter was fairly full, and the vent hose had a sagging bit full of fluff which I cleaned out. Still cold after 20 min. It's a vented one so no condenser. What part do I need then?

The issue is probably a failed component inside. On a Beko vented dryer of this age, the most likely cause is the heater element itself having burned out (gone open-circuit). I cannot tell you exactly which part to buy without a multimeter test because these components are located behind the rear panel and require dismantling. Checking the heater element on a 6-year-old dryer is often not cost-effective compared to buying a new machine, unless you are handy with tools and can source the parts cheaply. 1. You will need to unplug the dryer and remove the rear panel (usually held by screws).
2. Locate the heater element (a metal coil assembly) and the thermal cut-out (a small sensor clipped nearby).
3. A multimeter check for continuity on these parts is required to confirm which one has failed. If you are not comfortable with this level of dismantling or testing, I would recommend calling a qualified appliance engineer to diagnose it definitively, or considering replacement of the unit.

candidates: Blocked lint filter tripping the thermal cut-out (high)
Failed heater element or thermal cut-out (medium)
